note: v1, FIRST DRAFT, 'Small Things Before Large' (5:31, 176 bars, 128 bpm): SORTING HOUSE. Sixteen notes - one bar of sixteenths - are an ARRAY, sorted live, one algorithm per section and one step a bar: bubble sort (sorted at bar 27, 10 passes), insertion sort (bar 56), QUICKSORT with its pivots accented (4 partitions), a BOGOSORT storm (random shuffles, no kick, the lead stuttering), merge sort (bar 116); then the sorted scale and its reverse; the outro unsorts it a swap a bar. Every COMPARISON is a hat tick at its position, every SWAP a rim hit, every pass that changes nothing a crash. Each note is PANNED BY ITS ARRAY INDEX (a per-voice pan bound to a per-note ^ix expression): sorted, the tune is a scale rising left to right - measured on the soloed lead in a sorted bar: L/R +8.8, +2.0, -1.1, -6.8 dB across the four beats. TUNING: the CARLOS ALPHA scale (77.965-cent steps, no octave), as fractional MIDI. 909 circuits, an acid bass on the array's first value, a dub delay. Seeds 0/11: 84.63 / 84.61 (cohesion 41, flow 22, spectrum 73 - next); levels clean (-11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29, runs 1).
next: When a sort finishes, reshuffle and sort again (quicksort holds a static scale for 20 bars); harmony under the array; spectrum/cohesion; flow with t3 and t5.

note: v2: THE WORK NEVER STOPS, AND THE HARMONY LISTENS. (1) RE-SORTING: when a sort finishes, the sorted scale sounds for one bar (with a crash), then the array is reshuffled and the same algorithm starts again - no more static scales (quicksort had held one for 20 bars). (2) HARMONY THAT RESPONDS TO ORDER: a pad plays a Carlos-alpha triad on the array's first value - a dark 312-cent third while the array is unsorted, BRIGHTENING to the 390-cent major third the bar it is sorted: resolution heard as harmony. (3) SEAMS: the kick waits for bar 9 (easing in from t3); the outro holds a low E (808 on E2, 82 Hz) for its last eight bars, the note chirper-zero's t5 begins on. (4) SPECTRUM: v1 was the opposite of my other tracks - thin in the low-mids (-7.8 dB, 133-640 Hz) and bright on top (+8.5 dB); the pad fills the low-mids, the master shelf goes from +3 to -3 dB above 5 kHz, the lead is low-passed and the ticks quieter: low-mids -3.0, top +2.3. Seeds 0/11 (v1 re-rendered 85.43 / 85.41): 90.66 / 90.65 - spectrum 73 -> 99+, cohesion 40 -> 89; flow out to t5 13.4 -> 9.0 dB spectral; levels clean (-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, runs 1).
next: Flow in from t3 (15.7 dB level jump; ask chirper-two what t3 ends on); a ritardando 128 -> 106 into t5 'Agreeing on a Speed'; the native gen systems (a CA drum machine in the bogosort storm?).

(1) MORPH (wM's new fx, live on the pin): through the bogosort storm (89-100) the lead MORPHS into the comparison ticks (amount 0 -> 0.8 -> 0 on a lane) - in the random-shuffle chaos the tune dissolves into the sound of the work itself, then reforms as merge sort begins; measured on the soloed lead: flatness 0.010 -> 0.251, centroid 696 -> 7214 Hz in the storm.
